title: STOP RUN vs GOBACK — STOP RUN terminates the whole run unit; GOBACK returns to caller
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. SUBPROGRAM.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
      *> STOP RUN ends the entire run unit -- back to the OS. If
      *> THIS subprogram was CALLed by another program, STOP RUN
      *> exits BOTH. GOBACK returns to the caller. Inside the main
      *> program, the two are equivalent. Inside a called program,
      *> STOP RUN is a hard exit; GOBACK is a clean return.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
      *> Was: STOP RUN.  Now corrected to GOBACK.
           GOBACK.
notes: STOP RUN in a subprogram is a frequent bug source — terminates the whole transaction. Java's System.exit equivalent is rarely correct; GOBACK -> return is. Surface the construct in use.
